items.prompt: White's rook is already on the seventh rank, the Black king is on g8 and White has a pawn on d6. White to move. Can White win with best play?

claims.statement: The position is a win for White (tablebase, exact).
If it were Black's turn, the king on g8 could go only to f8 and h8.
The pawn on d6 is a passed pawn.

hints: Count the squares the Black king has while the rook holds the seventh rank.
Look at how far the pawn has come and whether anything can stop it from the front.
The king is cut off and the pawn is far advanced, so the rank works here.
items.explain: Tablebase (exact): White wins. The king on g8 has only f8 and h8 because the rook holds the seventh rank, and the pawn on d6 is passed and far advanced. Both conditions hold here.

items.prompt: The pawn stands on d5 instead of d6; everything else is the same. White to move. Can White win with best play?

claims.statement: The position is a draw (tablebase, exact).
The king on g8 still has only f8 and h8 if it were Black's turn.
The pawn on d5 is a passed pawn.

hints: Compare with the last position: the pawn is one step less advanced.
The king is still confined and the rook is still on the seventh.
With the king on g8, a pawn on d5 is not far enough forward.
items.explain: Tablebase (exact): a draw. The rook still holds the seventh and the king still has two squares, but the pawn is one step less advanced. A rook on the seventh does not decide the game by itself. With the king in the corner the same pawn wins (see the h8 position later).

items.explain: Tablebase (exact): still a win. Moving the Black rook from a1 to a8 does not change the result here, so it is not the feature that matters.
